ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in rectangle $ABCD$, where $AB=3$ and $AD=5$, point $E$ is on $DC$. When rectangle $ABCD$ is folded along $AE$, point $D$ falls exactly on point $F$ on side $BC$. What is the value of $\cos\angle EFC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given the properties of reflection transformations, we know that $\angle AFE = \angle D = 90^\circ$, and AF = AD = 5,\\
$\therefore \angle EFC + \angle AFB = 90^\circ$,\\
$\because \angle B = 90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BAF + \angle AFB = 90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle EFC = \angle BAF$,\\
$\cos \angle BAF = \frac{BA}{BF} = \frac{3}{5}$,\\
$\therefore \cos \angle EFC = \boxed{\frac{3}{5}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Figure description: In the figure is rectangle ABCD, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, D is at the upper right; E is located on the right side DC, F is located on the bottom side BC. In the figure AE, AF, EF are drawn, indicating that after folding along AE, the original point D falls onto F on side BC, forming triangle AFE. Given AB=3, AD=5. Reasoning: Folding is a reflection transformation, and lengths and angles remain unchanged. D is folded to F, and A and E remain fixed on the crease AE, so AD corresponds to AF, therefore AF=AD=5; originally vertex D of the rectangle was a right angle, so after folding the corresponding \angle AFE=90^\circ, that is, AF \perp EF. Also because F, B, C are on the same straight line BC, so at point F, \angle EFC and \angle AFB are complementary. On the other hand, in triangle ABF, AB \perp BF, so \angle BAF and \angle AFB are also complementary. Therefore \angle EFC=\angle BAF. Thus \cos\angle EFC=\cos\angle BAF. In right triangle ABF, AF=5 is the hypotenuse, and AB=3 is the adjacent side of \angle BAF, so \cos\angle BAF=\frac{AB}{AF}=\frac{3}{5}. Therefore \cos\angle EFC=\frac{3}{5}.
